s1.syndrome_frame: Ocular inflammation with eyelid involvement and conjunctival hyperemia in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
key_facts: Switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

shortlist.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has biopsy-proven Crohn disease and is experiencing ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Infliximab-induced ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was initially on infliximab therapy, which can cause ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse, and adalimumab can also cause ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Blepharitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins

shortlist.label: Sjögren's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has autoimmune disease (Crohn disease) and is experiencing ocular inflammation, which can be associated with Sjögren's syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms improved after discontinuation of TNF-α inhibitor treatment, suggesting a link between the medication and the ocular inflammation
raw.anchor_refutation: Blepharitis is a general term for eyelid inflammation, but the specific temporal relationship between the TNF-α inhibitor treatment and the onset of symptoms points towards a drug-induced cause rather than a primary blepharitis

rejected.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
rejected.why: While the patient has Crohn disease, the specific pattern of eyelid involvement and response to treatment discontinuation suggests a more direct link to the medication

rejected.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
rejected.why: The patient was switched to adalimumab after infliximab due to disease relapse, but the symptoms were present during infliximab treatment, making it a more likely culprit

rejected.label: Blepharitis
rejected.why: As explained in the anchor refutation, the temporal relationship between the TNF-α inhibitor treatment and the onset of symptoms suggests a more specific cause than primary blepharitis

rejected.label: Sjögren's syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic symptoms or other criteria that would suggest Sjögren's syndrome, making it an unlikely diagnosis in this case
